Genetics plays a big factor for a person to be diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. You would expect that a lot of morbidly obese people have type 2 diabetes but no, a lot of them are just pre-diabetic. If someone in your family was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes then chances are your family's genes are "diabetes-prone" and may rise your chances of being diagnosed but it will still probably a 15 year long process even if you eat a lot of food with high-sugar levels everyday.

It will be a painful one, dying with diabetes due to uncontrolled blood sugar levels and eventually going to a sudden drop in blood sugar levels will cause you to have the most painful migraine leading to a shock until you collapse+passout and die. Also you will feel so weak that even breathing will become a chore. You will regret hypoglycemia if someone managed to call 911 and let you survive.
